connections.why: The family is a primary agency of socialisation introduced in the core theme
Youth subcultures are a context for forming identity through socialisation
The media is an increasingly powerful agent of secondary socialisation
Concepts of culture and identity frame the questions sociologists research
Research methods are applied to investigate patterns of inequality
Identity categories such as class, gender and ethnicity structure inequality
Methodological skills support the synoptic study of globalisation
Inequality shapes how crime is distributed and explained across society
Class, gender and ethnic inequalities are central to educational achievement
Religion intersects with inequalities of class, gender and ethnicity
Globalisation reshapes crime through transnational and digital forms
Global forces influence education policy and the experience of schooling
Globalisation affects religious belief, fundamentalism and secularisation
The media are central to the digital and global social world
Youth subcultures connect to debates on deviance and social control
Family socialisation transmits the inequalities studied in this unit
